title: 232. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Mixture Problems with Linear Equations
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Form a linear equation for mixing two solutions with different concentrations.
questions.question: A chemist mixes \(x\) liters of a \(10\%\) saline solution with \(20\) liters of a \(30\%\) saline solution. The resulting mixture is \(25\%\) saline. Which equation represents this situation?
questions.explanation:
The amount of salt from the \(10\%\) solution is \(0.10x\), and the amount of salt from the \(20\) liters of \(30\%\) solution is \(0.30(20)=6\). The total volume is \(x+20\), and the final mixture is \(25\%\) saline, so its salt content is \(0.25(x+20)\). Therefore the equation is
\[
0.10x+0.30(20)=0.25(x+20)
\]
questions.hint: Equate the total salt from the two solutions to the salt in the final mixture, using \(\text{concentration}\times\text{volume}\).

questions.learningObjective: Form a linear equation for mixing two acid solutions to obtain a target concentration.
questions.question: A \(30\%\) acid solution is mixed with a \(50\%\) acid solution to make \(40\) liters of a \(42\%\) acid solution. If \(x\) is the number of liters of the \(30\%\) solution, which equation represents this situation?
questions.explanation:
If \(x\) liters are taken from the \(30\%\) solution, then \(40-x\) liters must be taken from the \(50\%\) solution. The total acid is
\[
0.30x+0.50(40-x)
\]
The final mixture is \(40\) liters at \(42\%\) acid, so its acid content is \(0.42(40)\). Therefore the equation is
\[
0.30x+0.50(40-x)=0.42(40)
\]
questions.hint: Use the fact that the two amounts together must equal the final total volume.

questions.learningObjective: Form a linear equation for adding water to dilute a solution.
questions.question: Let \(x\) be the number of liters of pure water added to \(8\) liters of a \(75\%\) acid solution to reduce it to a \(50\%\) acid solution. Which equation represents this situation?
questions.explanation:
The original solution contains \(0.75(8)=6\) liters of acid. Adding \(x\) liters of pure water does not change the amount of acid, but the total volume becomes \(8+x\). The final mixture is \(50\%\) acid, so the acid content is \(0.50(8+x)\). Therefore the equation is
\[
0.75(8)=0.50(8+x)
\]
questions.hint: The amount of acid remains unchanged when only water is added.

questions.learningObjective: Form a linear equation for mixing two salt solutions to obtain a target concentration.
questions.question: A \(12\%\) salt solution is mixed with a \(20\%\) salt solution to make \(10\text{ kg}\) of an \(18\%\) salt solution. If \(x\text{ kg}\) is the amount of the \(12\%\) solution, which equation represents this situation?
questions.explanation:
If \(x\text{ kg}\) is taken from the \(12\%\) solution, then \((10-x)\text{ kg}\) must be taken from the \(20\%\) solution. The total salt is
\[
0.12x+0.20(10-x)
\]
The final mixture is \(10\text{ kg}\) at \(18\%\) salt, so its salt content is \(0.18(10)\). Therefore the equation is
\[
0.12x+0.20(10-x)=0.18(10)
\]
questions.hint: Use \(10-x\) for the amount of the second solution, since the total final mass is \(10\text{ kg}\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the amount of one solution needed to obtain a target concentration.
questions.question: How many liters of a \(40\%\) alcohol solution must be mixed with a \(60\%\) alcohol solution to obtain \(20\) liters of a \(45\%\) alcohol solution?
questions.explanation:
Let \(x\) be the number of liters of the \(40\%\) solution. Then \(20-x\) liters of the \(60\%\) solution are used. The total alcohol is
\[
0.40x+0.60(20-x)
\]
The final mixture is \(20\) liters at \(45\%\) alcohol, so its alcohol content is \(0.45(20)=9\). Thus
\[
0.40x+0.60(20-x)=9
\]
Expanding gives \(0.40x+12-0.60x=9\), so \(-0.20x=-3\), and \(x=15\). Therefore \(15\) liters of the \(40\%\) solution are needed.
questions.hint: Let \(x\) be the amount of the \(40\%\) solution, then use \(20-x\) for the other solution.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the amount of a lower-concentration solution needed in a mixture.
questions.question: A \(5\%\) saline solution and a \(10\%\) saline solution are mixed to make \(12\) liters of an \(8\%\) saline solution. How many liters of the \(5\%\) solution are needed?
questions.explanation:
Let \(x\) be the number of liters of the \(5\%\) solution. Then \(12-x\) liters of the \(10\%\) solution are used. The total salt is
\[
0.05x+0.10(12-x)
\]
The final mixture is \(12\) liters at \(8\%\) salt, so its salt content is \(0.08(12)=0.96\). Thus
\[
0.05x+0.10(12-x)=0.96
\]
Expanding gives \(0.05x+1.2-0.10x=0.96\), so \(-0.05x=-0.24\), and \(x=4.8\). Therefore \(4.8\) liters of the \(5\%\) solution are needed.
questions.hint: Set the total salt from the two solutions equal to the salt in the final mixture.

questions.concept: Mixture equation with addition of a component
questions.learningObjective: Determine the amount of a component to add to reach a target percentage.
questions.question: A snack mix contains \(30\%\) peanuts and \(70\%\) raisins. How many kilograms of peanuts must be added to \(20\text{ kg}\) of this mix to make a mixture that is \(50\%\) peanuts?
questions.explanation:
The \(20\text{ kg}\) mix contains \(0.30(20)=6\text{ kg}\) of peanuts. Let \(x\) be the kilograms of peanuts added. The total peanuts become \(6+x\), and the total mass becomes \(20+x\). Since the new mixture is \(50\%\) peanuts,
\[
6+x=0.50(20+x)
\]
Expanding gives \(6+x=10+0.50x\), so \(0.50x=4\), and \(x=8\). Therefore \(8\text{ kg}\) of peanuts must be added.
questions.hint: The amount of peanuts increases by \(x\), while the total mass also increases by \(x\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the amount of pure acid needed to reach a target concentration.
questions.question: A \(20\%\) acid solution is mixed with pure acid to produce \(10\) liters of a \(50\%\) acid solution. How many liters of pure acid are needed?
questions.explanation:
Let \(x\) be the liters of pure acid. Then \(10-x\) liters of the \(20\%\) solution are used. The total acid is
\[
0.20(10-x)+x
\]
The final mixture is \(10\) liters at \(50\%\) acid, so its acid content is \(0.50(10)=5\). Thus
\[
0.20(10-x)+x=5
\]
Expanding gives \(2-0.20x+x=5\), so \(0.80x=3\), and \(x=3.75\). Therefore \(3.75\) liters of pure acid are needed.
questions.hint: Pure acid has concentration \(100\%\), so its acid contribution is \(x\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the amount of an alloy needed to reach a target copper percentage.
questions.question: How many kilograms of an alloy that is \(80\%\) copper must be melted with \(20\text{ kg}\) of an alloy that is \(30\%\) copper to obtain an alloy that is \(50\%\) copper?
questions.explanation:
Let \(x\) be the kilograms of the \(80\%\) copper alloy. The \(20\text{ kg}\) of \(30\%\) copper alloy contains \(0.30(20)=6\text{ kg}\) of copper. The total copper is
\[
0.80x+6
\]
The total mass is \(x+20\), and the final alloy is \(50\%\) copper, so
\[
0.80x+6=0.50(x+20)
\]
Expanding gives \(0.80x+6=0.50x+10\), so \(0.30x=4\), and \(x=\frac{40}{3}\). Therefore \(\frac{40}{3}\text{ kg}\) of the \(80\%\) alloy are needed.
questions.hint: Equate the total copper to \(50\%\) of the total final mass.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the amount of a solution needed when mixing with water.
questions.question: A \(10\%\) salt solution is mixed with water to produce \(30\) liters of a \(4\%\) salt solution. How many liters of the \(10\%\) salt solution are needed?
questions.explanation:
Let \(x\) be the liters of the \(10\%\) salt solution. Then \(30-x\) liters of water are used. The salt comes only from the \(10\%\) solution, so the total salt is \(0.10x\). The final mixture is \(30\) liters at \(4\%\) salt, so its salt content is \(0.04(30)=1.2\). Thus
\[
0.10x=1.2
\]
Solving gives \(x=12\). Therefore \(12\) liters of the \(10\%\) salt solution are needed.
questions.hint: Water contains no salt, so all salt in the final mixture comes from the \(10\%\) solution.
